decisions.quote: We set out to replicate the psychologically induced cooling of the stimulated hand during the RHI reported by Moseley et al. [ 2 ] in three consecutive experiments, comparing different experimental procedures. While we could not replicate the results at all with the automated stroking procedure (used in [ 13 ]), it was possible to replicate the result using a manual stroking procedure, albeit in both the experimental and the control condition.
decisions.reason: Across three experiments re-testing Moseley et al. (2008), the authors explicitly state that they could not replicate the cooling effect in the automated stroking procedures (Experiments 1 and 2) but replicated relative cooling of the stimulated hand using the manual stroking procedure (Experiment 3), albeit in both the experimental and control conditions and without the original correlation with ownership vividness.

parent_objection: First reply calls the three experiments mixed: no cooling with automated stroking,but manual-stroking cooling in both illusion and control conditions. Discussion then explicitly says cooling is independent of subjective ownership,requires a specific procedure,and is not strictly psychologically induced by the RHI as proposed by Moseley2008. Determine whether the paper main message is a methodological/construct-validity critique warranting statistically successful but flawed after recovering cooling,an overall failed test of the original ownership-specific causal claim,or an actual mixed verdict. Do not equate any hand cooling with replication of psychologically induced cooling,or infer category solely from counts of experiments. Follow authors own overall verdict and main-message scope; inspect full abstract,Discussion,and conclusion. Type and Moseley2008 identity remain settled.
